editorial.summary: David Choe and Harry Kim restart Thumbs Up in Tijuana, return to Los Angeles through a border rail yard, briefly visit David's parents and head north toward Alaska by truck, hitchhiking and freight train. The episode holds its own strongest counterevidence: unsupervised testosterone injection is followed by sickness; a police officer and rail worker both warn them away from dangerous track behavior before they plan to board a moving train; and shelter seeking becomes admitted breaking and entering. The Fresno warehouse ends in an extended, speculative reading of explicit graffiti. The editorial layer preserves every idea and source-era term while keeping medical risk, coercive language, illegality, private family/driver identities, speculation and publisher speaker-label provenance separate from literal transcript text.
